subject: APAC region pinning — temporary cross-zone sync policy & subprocessor visibility
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthlytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC region pinning — temporary cross-zone sync policy & subprocessor visibility

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking a look. We're finalizing our procurement checklist for HealthyLytics' rollout in APAC and have a couple of specific asks before we sign the DPA:

1) Region pinning: We need confirmation that customer data for our APAC tenant will remain physically in APAC under normal operations.
2) Temporary cross-zone sync: We understand occasional transient replication may occur for replication/DR (e.g., between Singapore and Tokyo edge nodes). Can you spell out the max window for such transient sync, whether data is logged, and any conditions that trigger it?
3) Subprocessor visibility: We need a recent roster of subprocessors that may touch APAC data and whether any of them are outside APAC for short durations.

I've attached a copy of the draft DPA (HealthyLytics_DPA_v1.2.pdf) with the clauses our legal team wants clarified.

Appreciate a short written response we can share with our legal/procurement and, if needed, a technical run-through.

Best,
Daniel
Director, Platform Ops
HealthyLytics

[attachment: HealthyLytics_DPA_v1.2.pdf]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC region pinning — temporary cross-zone sync policy & subprocessor visibility

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: Redwood supports APAC region pinning as a first-class configuration; we also have well-defined, time-limited transient-sync guardrails for disaster recovery scenarios. Below are the specifics you can share with procurement and legal.

On region pinning
- Normal operations: Customer data is served and stored in APAC regions (Singapore, Tokyo) per the APAC tenancy. Models and inference state (KV cache) remain in-customer-region by default.
- Non-customer-visible metadata (routing telemetry) is minimized and pseudonymized; we can provide a telemetry schema on request.

On temporary cross-zone sync (transient replication)
- Purpose: failover, short-lived cache warmup, and scheduled migration maintenance.
- Conditions that trigger: full-zone outage (SLA threshold breach), planned maintenance with prior notice, or emergency failover declared by Redwood ops.
- Max window without explicit written authorization: 72 hours. We record start/end timestamps and k-v cache deltas.
- Logging & evidence: all transient syncs create an audit record (start_ts, end_ts, affected shards, destination zone) — we can surface these to your security team.

Subprocessor visibility
- Attached is our current APAC-focused subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_2028-04.csv). Note: a small set of edge providers may operate outside APAC for <72h transient failover; these are listed with purpose and country.

Next steps
- I've attached our APAC residency playbook for technical detail (APAC_residency_playbook.pdf).
- If your legal team wants explicit DPA language for the 72h transient window, we can propose text and mark it as an addendum to the DPA.
- Karthik, adding you for the DR/ops timeline and any technical caveats.

Happy to jump on a short call — what times look good for you this week?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, APAC Accounts
Redwood Inference

[attachment: APAC_residency_playbook.pdf]
[attachment: subprocessor_roster_2028-04.csv]

Thanks Tessa — this is great. A couple follow-ups from procurement/legal:

- Can you provide a sample audit extract showing the transient-sync audit record format (start_ts, end_ts, shards affected)?
- Are the <72-hour windows capped per incident or per month (i.e., could recurring short syncs exceed 72 hours aggregated)?
- Procurement asked whether we can get the subprocessor roster signed/acknowledged as part of the SOW annex.

If you can send the sample audit extract and confirm the aggregation question, we can move the DPA redlines into our legal queue.

Appreciate it — cc'd procurement and legal.

Daniel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC region pinning — temporary cross-zone sync policy & subprocessor visibility

Hi Daniel — Karthik from Redwood infra team here. Quick technical clarifications and a sample audit snippet below.

1) 72-hour window semantics
- The 72-hour limit is per incident/event (e.g., a single failover operation). We do not aggregate separate incidents into a rolling total for the purpose of that limit. However, recurring incidents would each be logged individually and surfaced to customers.

2) Sample audit extract (we can produce a CSV/JSON sample on request):
- event_id: evt-20280411-0441
- start_ts: 2028-04-11T03:21:10Z
- end_ts: 2028-04-11T06:04:35Z
- source_zone: ap-southeast1 (Singapore)
- dest_zone: ap-northeast1 (Tokyo)
- affected_shards: shard-3, shard-7
- reason: zonal outage (network fabric)
- operator: automated-failover

(If you prefer a redacted sample file we can attach it; we typically deliver a CSV export keyed to your account ID.)

3) Subprocessor roster & SOW annex
- We can include the APAC subprocessor roster as an annex to the DPA/SOW. Any subprocessors that may be used for transient failover are explicitly listed and scoped to the 72-hour incident policy.

4) Additional guardrails
- All transient-sync traffic is encrypted in transit and limited to replicas required for recovery.
- We retain transient-sync audit records for 12 months by default (longer retention is available as an add-on).

Next steps
- I'll prepare a redacted sample audit CSV and a proposed DPA addendum clause for the 72-hour transient window by EOD tomorrow and drop into the HubSpot deal (HL-4592).
- Tessa / Lauren: please propose 30 minutes tomorrow so we can walk procurement/legal through the extract.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
